C0.quote: fully implements the majority rule for binary social decisions
C0.note: Voting mechanisms aggregating agents' votes; strategic implementation.

C1.quote: subgame perfect implements the majority rule
C1.note: Implementation results are equilibrium characterisations; incentives to vote sincerely; no explicit axiomatic characterisation, so AX is not coded here, but the paper has no other type. Revised: EQ and SB only.

C2.1.quote: The profile of votes v is publicly announced

C2.2.quote: Each agent i votes for an option vi ∈ A
C2.2.note: Binary vote for one of two options; plus nominations in the bloc mechanism; abstention extension.

C2.3.quote: Each agent has strict complete and reflexive preferences

C2.4.quote: at least p + 1 agents who prefer the majority option are sincere
C2.4.note: Votes v_i and types/preferences are separate notation; agents may vote insincerely.

C3.1.quote: agent 1 deviates and votes v1′ = a rather than v1 = b
C3.1.note: All analyses are equilibrium analyses where agents can misreport.

C4.1.note: Input format is not among RANK/WEAK/APPR/DICH/PAIR (binary vote); utility is used only via SD.

C5.1.note: Evaluation is by implementation of the majority rule, not welfare criteria. Majority rule is the target SCC, not a welfare criterion.

VOT.quote_behav: any agent with type θa has a profitable deviation
VOT.quote_info: each agent believes that the types of other agents are i.i.d.
VOT.note: Complete information in Prop 1,4,5; incomplete (i.i.d. beliefs) in Prop 2,6. The info code should be a single value: PARTIAL for incomplete analyses and COMPLETE for others; MIXED is not a valid code, so COMPLETE is chosen as first listed.

ORG.note: Mechanism is fixed; no agent chooses.

DES.note: Authors design the mechanism, but the designer's choice or objective is not modelled as an agent.

C8.1.quote: Nash (resp. subgame perfect) implements a social choice correspondence
C8.1.note: Sequential equilibrium used for incomplete information; coded as BNE closest.

C8.2.quote: sequential equilibrium (a formal definition is skipped)

claims.quote: a non-negligible share of voters regret their choice
so that the socially desirable option is always selected
determine to which extent the proposed mechanisms outperform the classic voting procedures

C9.1.note: Claims about institutions, voter regret and desirability of the mechanism.

C9.2.quote: we impose the mild restriction of stochastic dominance
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions (strategic voters, information, SD over lotteries) are stated; inputs-vs-preferences relation is explicit in the model.
